recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Questioning Precession and the Fixed Star Dome", "body": "LC King said precession was a red flag because it was untestable for ordinary people, at 72 years per degree. He argued that the stars were fixed in a stable dome and that the position of the sun shaped how they were seen. He described three zodiac layouts, the old man, bull and lion version, the tropical and the sidereal, and said each worked as a seasonal check at a different time of day using Stellarium. Chance noted that he wanted to give LC a full InnerVerse episode to unpack the research, and said the precession idea came from untrustworthy sources."}, {"title": "Twin Cycles, Eight Spokes, and the Number Nine", "body": "Benjamin Balderson said LC's system could divide by twelve but ran on an eight part pattern like older pagan and heathen cultures, with a growth cycle and a death cycle running at once. One speaker compared this to movie heroes and villains who mirror each other across the year. One speaker argued that nine acted like a zero, so eight spokes surround a central ninth point, and another tied it to Sleipnir's eight legs. A further speaker described the Hermetic idea that the angel of death and the angel of life were the same sun."}, {"title": "The Galvanic Battery Model of Sun and Moon", "body": "LC King described the world as a galvanic cell, with sun and moon as opposite poles and a mercurial connection between them. He proposed that mercury was a planet former because of its surface tension and its ability to amalgamate metals. Ben explained that galvanic and electrolysis cycles reversed the roles of cathode and anode, so the sun's role was arbitrary. Chance connected this to the tarot, where the moon card is 18 and the sun is 19, and suggested that the cycles of those bodies pointed to a feminine sun and masculine moon, while allowing both readings."}, {"title": "Heimdall, Polaris, and the Perfect Seed", "body": "Ben told the story of Heimdall as the perfect white shining one, born of nine mothers, whose seed descended through nine chakras and gained density before rising again. He linked this to the Rainbow Bridge, where white light splits into colors. Ben also argued that Polaris never moved while the sun only hid it for part of each day, and that older cosmologies placed little importance on the sun. One speaker raised a wordplay between the son of nine virgins and the virgin of salvation, and said small tweaks in language could change an entire meaning."}, {"title": "Home Experiments, Farming, and Living Soil", "body": "Snake Jones asked what he could build at home, and LC suggested making a simple battery from fruit and trying electrolysis. Ben recommended colloidal silver and spark gap experiments, while LC pointed to the Geet engine, which he said he had built on a small petrol engine years ago. LC described his market garden in Victoria, Australia, his setup costs, and why he left a government job, and he called modern farming an anti life system. Ben passed along a microscope based soil course, and Chance praised the idea of the soil as the stomach of the plant."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Electrify the first day of Aquarius season with tonight's Vibe Rant, featuring the cosmological renegades Benjamin Balderson and LC King. Expect a laid back chat that challenges the conventional correlations of astrology and alchemy.
